if someone would be new to that kind of analysis, how would you describe Elliott Wave in simple sentences?
Well, okay, I think the simplest way to understand it is it's a description of the price patterns
that unfold over and over again in financial markets. So, Elliott Wave Theory is really the study
of these price patterns. So, you could imagine that understanding the way these patterns behave
might be of use to you if you're a trader or an investor. If we go back to the early 1930s when
Elliott Wave theory was developed, can you give us a bit of the backdrop? How did the connection
happened between the original, let me reface this again, sorry. Let's look back to the early 1930s
when the Elliott Wave Theory was developed first time. How did the connection happen between your
father and the person that originally developed it? Well, the person who originally developed Elliott
Wave Theory was RN, Elliott Ralph Nelson, Elliott, and he was an accountant and he actually became
ill and was bedridden for long period of time and during that time he spent hours and hours
every day pouring over market charts and he kept noticing these recurring patterns in price and time
and those patterns eventually became the Elliott Wave Principle which he later wrote about.
And he actually used the theory to pinpoint the moment at which the great depression, the great
crash of 29 ended and he started telling people that they should be buying the market at that time.
So he put it into practice quite readily from that point. My father, when he came across the
Elliott Wave Theory, believe it or not, the only way at that time, which was, I believe that was
in the 70s, to read about the theory was on microfilm because they didn't even have full books,
so the information about it that R and Elliott had written about was almost lost to history and of
course he had prints created from the microfilm and of course popularized it a lot during the 80s.
So we almost didn't recover this theory. When did Elliott Wave Theory really blow up? I mean
everybody on Wall Street knows Elliott Wave Theory. The heyday when it was most popular was in the
1980s. My father had predicted a repeat of the roaring 20s right around the late 70s and early 80s
which of course went against the consensus at that time which was mostly doom and gloom which is
completely understandable when you have interest rates at 18% and just very scary runaway inflation.
I think that was the worst, I think it's the worst inflationary period in US history. Aside from
maybe the continental I guess. So you talked about your father making that public as a book and then
going into this period where it gets known everywhere. How do you feel now a generation after that
taking that forward or how has your father convinced you that you should continue that road?
